claim: A closed store answering HTTP 200 with everything OutOfStock and unpriced RESET the failure counter, so the dormancy guard could never fire. Withdrawing PRICES is what separates 'closed' from 'sold out'.

body.decision: DEC-330 (2026-08-27). Emergency exception, shipped ff036ce, deployed and verified from /opt/dale/scrapers.
body.what: Heritage Fruit Trees shut online sales for 2026 on 08-24. It 503ed for two nights (guard working), then from 08-26 began answering HTTP 200 with the whole catalogue present, every product OutOfStock and unpriced: 378 products, 0 in stock, 1 priced. ok=true reset consecutive_failures to 0, so the dormancy guard shipped 08-24 could never fire and Heritage was being scraped nightly until the 2027 season.
body.cost_was_real: Runs got LONGER not shorter (432s on the last real day, then 1235s and 1245s) because a 503 fails fast and a 200 does not. ~20 min/night of pointless requests at a nursery Benedict has a relationship with. Scraping cost goodwill twice: Beewise (DEC-198) and Heaven On Earth, who threatened Consumer Affairs the same day.
body.not_a_data_defect: Checked the far end (DEC-270) before building a repair. The live page really serves HTTP 200 with schema.org/OutOfStock and no price. The scraper is CORRECT, Heritage genuinely has nothing buyable, and the published CC BY dataset is not lying. untrusted_nurseries() is deliberately UNTOUCHED: marking Heritage untrusted would suppress a zero that is true. The fix changes whether we scrape, never whether we believe.
body.fix: is_unproductive(rec) = ok AND products>0 AND in_stock==0 AND priced share < UNPRODUCTIVE_PRICED_SHARE (0.10). consecutive_failures and last_success_day count those alongside outright failures.
body.priced_condition_is_load_bearing: A nursery can sell out completely and still trade, and a trading store keeps its prices on the page (~100% priced). Withdrawing prices too is what separates 'closed' from 'sold out', and it protects the restock alerts that are the reason to scrape daily. Heritage is 1/378 = 0.3% against a 10% threshold.
body.base_rate_measured_not_chosen: Across 27 nurseries and 200 days of health records, ok runs with products>0 and in_stock==0 occurred EXACTLY TWICE, both Heritage on 08-26 and 08-27. Zero false positives in all history.
body.threshold_not_bent: Streak reads 4 today; 5 is required. One more unproductive night is still needed before it sleeps, so the constant was not tuned to make today's case fire today (DEC-323).
body.the_alarm_could_not_see_it: detect_scrape_anomalies.py gained a priced_collapse rule on 08-24, two days before this. It compares today's priced share to YESTERDAY'S, and yesterday (08-25) was a failure carrying no priced field, so the comparison was skipped; on 08-27 today equalled yesterday so nothing fired. The alarm built for this exact failure was structurally unable to see it because the collapse happened ACROSS an outage. Same family as DEC-325. Not fixed here (backlog at cap); belongs to DAL-292.
body.guard: 6 new tests in tests/test_dormancy.py: the exact production sequence, the sold-out-but-trading case that must NOT back off, pre-priced records that must never be judged retroactively, and that an unproductive run stays TRUSTED data. Proven to fail 3/3 under the old logic before being trusted to pass (DEC-326). Full suite 3,565 OK.
